pages.text: A dungeon is a complex $(l)dug under the ground$(): only its entrance shows on the surface, and $(l)ruins, remains and signs$() around it give it away.$(br2)From the central $(l)rotunda$(), the great stairs lead down to the $(l)boss arena$(). Three optional $(l)wings$() branch off: each one ends with a chamber held by a $(l)Rune Warden$(), and a fine treasure.
pages.title: Donjons

pages.text: The real prize is the $(l)vault$() behind the arena. Its walls look like the rest of the dungeon, but they are $(item)Warded Masonry$(): nothing can break them, on any of the six faces. Its door of $(item)Guardian Seals$() only opens when the boss dies, and the masonry then becomes ordinary bricks.$(br2)Plans and rooms change from one dungeon to the next.

Every boss attack is $(l)announced$(): a circle filling up on the ground (leave it before it is full), a ring running along the floor (jump over it), a marked line (step aside), a sweeping beam ($(l)hide behind a pillar$()).$(br2)At each phase the boss stops, invulnerable, then releases a wave: take a step back. The more players, the more health it has.
pages.title: Combats

pages.text: Unbreakable. Dissolves when the dungeon boss dies. Bosses never leave their arena: if you flee, they go back and slowly heal.
